inferences: The video may show a reveal/collapse timing problem, incorrect window bounds, or auto-hide registration fallback, but the public text does not distinguish these behaviors.
The 200% scale makes DPI conversion and monitor work-area calculations a plausible investigation branch, but there is no evidence that scaling is causal.

A taskbar auto-hide conflict is another plausible branch because the current implementation intentionally falls back to pinned mode when the taskbar owns the same edge; this is not confirmed for the reporter.
Older reports #46239 and #46589 requested the auto-hide feature, and #46239 was implemented by PR #48565; they are not duplicates of this post-implementation malfunction report.
Open issue #48466 concerns incorrect dock positioning on another display and includes separate scaling/topology evidence, but it does not establish that #50405 has the same cause.
issue_context.analysis: The current source narrows the relevant boundary but not the failing branch. DockSettingsPage.xaml binds the auto-hide toggle to SettingsViewModel.Dock_AutoHide. DockWindow.CreateAppBar chooses AppBar auto-hide, checks for a same-edge taskbar auto-hide conflict, and can fall back to pinned mode; UpdateAutoHideWindowPosition, ApplyAutoHideRect, and the reveal/collapse timers then control the visible geometry and animation. The existing DockSettingsAutoHideToggleTest verifies settings persistence only, not visual behavior at high DPI. The author must describe the observed failure and setup before a safe design can select among those paths.
